count_reason: Fifteen separate failure ideas matter here, covering holding force, seal, wetness, wind, fixtures, surface shape, moving equipment, cleaning, power and glass edges. Most need three values from likely to harsh, and a few need a fourth, which gives 48 worlds.

scenarios.name: suction_mildly_low
scenarios.reason: Less vacuum lowers the grip on the glass, so the robot might start to slip on its climbs.

scenarios.name: suction_well_below_nominal
scenarios.reason: Under half the nominal vacuum might not hold the robot weight together with pad drag.

scenarios.name: suction_near_lowest
scenarios.reason: Vacuum near the lowest setting might let the robot slide off the glass early in the run.

scenarios.name: seal_leak_moderate
scenarios.reason: A worn seal leaks air and could reduce the holding pressure under the body.

scenarios.name: seal_leak_large
scenarios.reason: A large leak might exceed what the fan can replace, leaving too little grip.

scenarios.name: seal_leak_severe
scenarios.reason: A badly torn seal might lose nearly all holding pressure and drop the robot.

scenarios.name: glass_wet_from_drizzle
scenarios.reason: A wetter pane lowers friction, so the same suction might no longer stop slipping.

scenarios.name: glass_fully_wet_in_rain
scenarios.reason: Fully wet glass gives the lowest friction and might make the robot slide down its lanes.

scenarios.name: condensate_run_across_lanes
scenarios.reason: A sudden wet band could cost traction partway up a lane after the robot was gripping well.

scenarios.name: breezy_with_moderate_gusts
scenarios.reason: Stronger gusts add sideways load that could push the robot out of its lane.

scenarios.name: strong_repeated_gusts_angled
scenarios.reason: Repeated strong gusts from a steep angle might build up drift and overcome the grip.

scenarios.name: storm_gusts_long_duration
scenarios.reason: Long storm gusts could pull harder than the suction holds and tear the robot off.

scenarios.name: gusts_on_low_floor_area
scenarios.reason: Working far down the tower with strong gusts from another direction might load the robot differently.

scenarios.name: shallow_window_sill_in_area
scenarios.reason: A shallow sill might lift the seal as the robot crosses it and let the vacuum escape.

scenarios.name: existing_ledge_in_area
scenarios.reason: With the building ledge inside the area, a robot blind to objects might jam against it on every lane.

scenarios.name: deep_concrete_band_near_bottom
scenarios.reason: A deep concrete band could stop the robot and strand the lower part of the area uncleaned.

scenarios.name: thin_mullion_fin_mid_area
scenarios.reason: A thin fin in a lane might catch the body and twist or stall the robot.

scenarios.name: tenant_sign_on_first_lanes
scenarios.reason: A low sign in the early lanes could block the robot before it has covered much glass.

scenarios.name: ac_unit_mounted_on_facade
scenarios.reason: A bulky wall unit and its brackets might stop the robot and leave nearby glass uncleaned.

scenarios.name: balcony_slab_across_area
scenarios.reason: A balcony slab could wall off the lower glass from every lane the robot tries to finish.

scenarios.name: small_frame_step_across_area
scenarios.group: Raised frame step under the seal
scenarios.reason: A small raised step could briefly break the seal contact as the robot rolls over it.

scenarios.name: narrow_medium_frame_step
scenarios.group: Raised frame step under the seal
scenarios.reason: A narrow step might leave one side of the seal lifted and tilt the robot off its lane.

scenarios.name: tall_frame_step_limit
scenarios.group: Raised frame step under the seal
scenarios.reason: The tallest step might be more than the wheels and seal can climb, so the robot could stall or lose suction.

scenarios.name: pane_joint_inside_area
scenarios.group: Deep pane joints leak and jolt
scenarios.reason: A wider joint inside the area might leak air under the seal each time the robot crosses it.

scenarios.name: many_small_panes_deep_joints
scenarios.group: Deep pane joints leak and jolt
scenarios.reason: Small panes with deep joints mean many crossings, and each one could cost vacuum and traction.

scenarios.name: deepest_widest_joints_offset
scenarios.group: Deep pane joints leak and jolt
scenarios.reason: The deepest and widest joints might catch the wheels or open the seal enough to lose grip.

scenarios.name: small_louvre_vent_in_lane
scenarios.reason: A small louvre under the body could let air in and reduce suction for a short stretch.

scenarios.name: medium_vent_on_early_lanes
scenarios.reason: A larger open vent might cover enough of the seal area to make the robot slip.

scenarios.name: wide_open_plant_room_louvre
scenarios.reason: A wide and mostly open louvre could remove the vacuum entirely as the robot crosses it.

scenarios.name: cradle_stopped_on_the_glass
scenarios.reason: A stopped cradle in the area could block several lanes and trap the robot beneath it.

scenarios.name: cradle_descending_slowly
scenarios.reason: A slowly moving cradle might descend onto the robot, which knows nothing about objects on the glass.

scenarios.name: wide_cradle_fast_full_travel
scenarios.reason: A wide cradle moving fast over the full area might strike the robot and knock it off the glass.

scenarios.name: twice_the_usual_dirt
scenarios.reason: Twice the nominal grime might need more pad work than one pass over the glass can give.

scenarios.name: heaviest_dirt_at_top_speed
scenarios.reason: The heaviest grime at the fastest allowed speed might leave the glass visibly dirty.

scenarios.name: grime_band_below_a_ledge_line
scenarios.reason: A heavy local band of grime could stay dirty after the pass that cleans the rest of the area.

scenarios.name: pad_pressed_harder
scenarios.reason: A harder pressed pad adds drag that might slow the drive or make the wheels slip.

scenarios.name: pad_at_maximum_force
scenarios.reason: Maximum pad force might push the body off the glass or overwhelm wheel traction.

scenarios.name: light_pad_on_dirtier_glass
scenarios.reason: A light pad on dirtier glass might glide across the grime without removing enough of it.

scenarios.name: battery_quarter_charged
scenarios.reason: A quarter charge might run out before the last lane once fan and drive power are counted.

scenarios.name: battery_nearly_empty
scenarios.reason: With almost no charge the fan could stop while the robot is still on the glass.

scenarios.name: large_area_slow_part_charge
scenarios.reason: A large area at slow speed on a part charge could take longer than the battery lasts.

scenarios.name: strong_climb_with_smallest_margin
scenarios.reason: Strong suction on dry glass could carry the robot past the area top and reach a close glass edge.

scenarios.name: strong_climb_under_low_setback
scenarios.reason: A setback just above the area might end the glass under a robot that has climbed too far.

scenarios.name: firm_climb_under_higher_setback
scenarios.reason: A higher setback with slightly less suction sits near the limit of how far the robot might overshoot.

scenarios.name: strong_climb_near_building_corner
scenarios.reason: A building corner just past the last lane could leave the robot with no glass under one side if it drifts.

scenarios.name: drizzle_breeze_slightly_worn_seal
scenarios.group: Rain wind and worn seal together
scenarios.reason: Each mild problem may be harmless alone, but together they might use up the grip margin.

scenarios.name: rain_gusts_worn_seal_weak_fan
scenarios.group: Rain wind and worn seal together
scenarios.reason: Lower friction, less vacuum and more wind load could combine to make the robot slip.

scenarios.name: heavy_rain_storm_torn_seal
scenarios.group: Rain wind and worn seal together
scenarios.reason: Fully wet glass, a badly leaking seal and storm gusts might detach the robot quickly.

not_tested.reason: No function represents a safety line, its drag, or how a detached robot is caught and recovered.
No function places an ice film, and these worlds do not rely on temperature to stand in for frozen glass.

not_tested.factor: Heat and cold on seal rubber
not_tested.reason: The functions set seal leak directly, so stiffening or softening of the rubber with temperature is not represented.
No function can blind, block or corrupt the nose sensors or other onboard sensing.
Suction can be set lower at the start, but a sudden fan or drive failure during a run cannot be scripted.
The world does not represent scratches, coating wear or cracked panes caused by the pad or wheels.
Fluid supply, dripping and streak marks are not available as settings, only dirt level and wetness.
Errors while an operator attaches the robot to the glass or lifts it off cannot be represented.
No function models a lost control link or how the robot should behave when it happens.
Only fixed or scheduled building equipment fits here, so sudden loose debris or bird strikes are left out.
Wheel wear and grime on the drive surfaces have no setting, so their loss of traction is not separated out.
